findings.summary: gh_api() has no --max-time/--connect-timeout at all, while gitea_api() got --max-time 1800 (with data) / 60 (without). The brief explicitly says to 'bound how long any single request can run' — that requirement was applied to one helper and skipped for the other. Verified by inspection: the gh_api curl invocation (lines 61-66) carries no timeout flag, unlike both branches of gitea_api (lines 75 and 82).

findings.summary: Implementer report claims 'tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff touches only this one file — no test file was added or modified anywhere in the repo. The repo has an established convention for exactly this (scripts/tests/deploy-pull.test.sh, scripts/tests/backup-services-sync.test.sh: self-contained bash tests that stub external commands like curl/docker and assert on captured output), and this change is precisely the kind of subshell/status-propagation logic that convention exists to regression-guard. Either the claim is inflated or the tests were run ad hoc and discarded, leaving no durable check against the exact class of bug (status lost across command substitution) the brief describes.
